sections.title: EBS Volumes, Delete-on-Termination and Snapshots
keyTopics: Snapshot to move volume across AZ
sections.objective: Explain how EBS volumes attach, are locked to an AZ, are billed, and how snapshots, archive tier, recycle bin and FSR solve backup, migration and restore-latency requirements.

sections.title: AMIs and EC2 Instance Store
keyTopics: Instance store buffer and cache use cases
sections.objective: Choose between AMI-based pre-packaged launches and EC2 Instance Store for high-IOPS, ephemeral workloads, and state why instance store data is lost on stop or hardware failure.

sections.title: EBS Volume Types and Multi-Attach
keyTopics: io1 and io2 Block Express PIOPS
sections.objective: Select the EBS volume type matching IOPS, throughput, latency and cost needs, and decide when io1/io2 Multi-Attach with a cluster-aware file system is appropriate.

sections.title: EBS Encryption and Amazon EFS
keyTopics: EBS encryption at rest and in flight
Encrypting an unencrypted volume via snapshot
EBS vs EFS vs Instance Store
sections.objective: Explain EBS encryption at rest and its snapshot-based re-encryption path, then choose EFS versus EBS versus Instance Store based on multi-AZ sharing, OS compatibility, performance mode and cost.

notes: Page 109 is a summary slide linking to AWS docs; folded into the volume-types section. Page 104 is a diagram-only slide about instance store IOPS, kept with pages 103/105 context. Exam emphasis: Task 3.1 high-performance storage (instance store vs gp3 vs io2 latency/IOPS), Task 4.1 cost (gp3 vs gp2 sizing, st1/sc1 vs SSD, EFS IA/Archive, Snapshot Archive), Task 1.3 encryption at rest (KMS, snapshot copy encryption, EFS encryption). Distractors to expect: attaching an EBS volume across AZs, HDD as boot volume, Windows on EFS, gp2 IOPS raised independently of size, Multi-Attach on gp3.
